supplier_statement_guard:
Let U⊂R^n be open and Y:U→R^n be C¹. There is a unique maximal flow Φ on an open domain
D⊂R×U containing {0}×U, and Φ is jointly C¹. Its time slices are local C¹
diffeomorphisms with inverse Φ_{−t}; $\partial_t\Phi=Y(\Phi)$ and $D_p\Phi$ is the
unique solution V of $V′=DY(\Phi)V$, V(0)=I. Each regular point has a C¹ flow box. If Y
is C², Φ and those flow boxes are C²; the second state variation W satisfies
$W′=DY(\Phi)W+D²Y(\Phi)[Ve_i,Ve_j]$, W(0)=0. Individual trajectories of a C¹ field are
C² in time. A trajectory remaining in a compact K⊂⊂U cannot have a finite maximal
endpoint. These Euclidean conclusions use no full AC or DC.

operations.source_fact_guard: [F2] A $C^1$ autonomous field has a unique maximal $C^1$ flow with $\partial_t\phi_t(x)=f(\phi_t(x))$ ([[lem-c1-euclidean-maximal-flow-with-c2-upgrade]]). Uniqueness gives $\phi_T(\phi_s(x_*))=\phi_{T+s}(x_*)$ wherever both sides are defined: as functions of the elapsed time, both sides solve the same IVP from $\phi_s(x_*)$.
operations.old_quote:
Let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open and let $V:U\to\mathbb R^n$ be smooth. For
every $x_0\in U$ there exist $h>0$ and an open neighbourhood $W\subseteq U$ of
$x_0$ such that:

1. for every $y\in W$ there is a unique solution $\Phi(\,\cdot\,,y)$ of
   $x'=V(x)$ on $[-h,h]$ with $\Phi(0,y)=y$;
2. the map
   $$\Phi:(-h,h)\times W\to U,\qquad \Phi(t,y)=\Phi_t(y),$$
   is smooth in $y$ and $C^1$ in $t$, with
   $\partial_t\Phi(t,y)=V(\Phi(t,y))$ and $\Phi(0,y)=y$.

This is the local smooth flow of the autonomous vector field $V$.

operations.source_fact_guard: [F5] The monodromy is the state derivative of the flow ([[def-local-periodic-orbit-poincare-and-floquet-data]]). For the $C^2$ field in [F1], the finite-regularity maximal-flow theorem supplies a $C^2$ flow with time derivative $\partial_t\phi_t(x)=f(\phi_t(x))$ ([[lem-c1-euclidean-maximal-flow-with-c2-upgrade]]).

operations.source_fact_guard: [F6] The $C^2$ autonomous field supplied by the orbit certificate has a unique maximal $C^2$ flow with time derivative $f(\phi_t(x))$ ([[lem-c1-euclidean-maximal-flow-with-c2-upgrade]]). Uniqueness identifies a shifted trajectory with the solution from its shifted initial state, giving the flow law on the common domain. Composition derivatives obey the chain rule ([[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]]). Eigenvalues, algebraic multiplicities, and generalized vectors have the matrix meanings of [[def-eigenvalue-eigenvector-eigenspace-and-spectrum]] and [[thm-jordan-form-exists-iff-the-characteristic-polynomial-splits]].
